headline: Documentary Revives the Forgotten Legacy of Football's First Woman
meta_description: Filmmaker Ashley Brandon uses Barbie dolls and archival footage to tell the remarkable story of Pat Palinkas, who became the first woman to play professional f…
summary_short: A new Oscar-qualified documentary uses creative stop-motion animation to resurrect the nearly forgotten story of Pat Palinkas, who made history as the first woman to pla…
body:
In 1970, an elementary school teacher named Pat Palinkas stepped onto the field for the Orlando Panthers and became the first woman to play professional football—a milestone that made national headlines before fading into obscurity for more than five decades. Now, filmmaker Ashley Brandon's 12-minute documentary "Panther Pat" is restoring her legacy to view. The film, which won the Grand Jury Prize for Documentary Short at the 2026 Slamdance Film Festival and is Oscar-qualified, pairs interviews with Palinkas and archival material with an inventive creative choice: scenes staged using dolls, toys, and stop-motion animation. The project has drawn notable backing, with Eli Manning and Robin Roberts recently joining as executive producers.

Brandon discovered Palinkas's story by accident. While reading a used book about Connecticut football history, she found a single passing sentence mentioning Palinkas's game against the Bridgeport Jets—buried near the end as though it were a footnote rather than a watershed moment. Intrigued, Brandon tracked down Palinkas in Clearwater, Florida, and the two began collaborating in 2021. When archival footage proved scarce, Brandon embraced an unconventional solution: remembering how Palinkas had been told that "girls play with dolls," the filmmakers bought Barbies and toys to visually tell the story. What began as a budget-conscious workaround became the film's signature voice, allowing it to reach audiences beyond sports enthusiasts.

Palinkas died in summer 2025, months before completion, but her family has embraced the project. Brandon believes the playful doll-centered approach suits a woman who spent her career teaching elementary school—and hopes it will help young viewers see themselves reflected in Pat's groundbreaking achievement. "You can do it," Brandon says of the film's message. "Pat did it, so of course you can do it too."
